findings_qualitative.value: Forthcoming ALMA observations of GS-z14-0 (3σ sensitivity 18 µJy/beam) will come very close to constraining the fiducial prediction (14.9 µJy) of the outflow-based attenuation-free model and can detect dust-rich scenarios.

evidence.quote: Forthcoming ALMA observations, with an expected 3 σ sensitivity of 18 µ Jy, should come very close to constraining the fiducial predictions of the outflow-based attenuation-free model.

findings_qualitative.value: If dust in GS-z14-0 is not ejected and remains within r_e, the high optical depth and high temperature (~100-125 K) suppress the 88 µm flux to <= 5.3 µJy, or require a very small dust-to-stellar mass ratio (log ξ_d < -4.2) to match A_V = 0.31.

evidence.quote: These two properties act as to dramatically suppress the flux: independently of ξ d (unless extremely small), F 88 = 5 . 3 µ Jy.

If the dust is in the galaxy ( r d = r e ) its temperature is 110 − 125 K. In this case, though, the dustto stellar mass ratio must be very small (log ξ d < − 4 . 2) not to exceed the measured A V = 0 . 31.

findings_qualitative.value: If early dust is predominantly composed of large (~0.5 µm) silicate grains, the dust is colder and the predicted 88 µm flux is smaller (9.5 µJy for GS-z14-0) and more compact.

evidence.quote: The temperature follows the same trend as in the standard case, but it is significantly colder, reaching at r e values in the range 75 − 85 K. As a result, for any given ξ d , the flux is smaller, e.g. F 88 fid = 9 . 5 µ Jy, and shifted to smaller radii compared to the standard case.

findings_qualitative.value: Other z > 10 galaxies (GS-z14-1, UNCOVER-z12, GS-z11-0, GHZ2) are predicted to be fainter at 88 µm (fiducial fluxes 2 - 5.2 µJy) than GS-z14-0 due to lower SFRs and lower A_V.

evidence.quote: Other super-early galaxies are predicted (Tab. 1) to be fainter at 88 µ m, mostly because of their lower SFR compared to GS-z14-0 but also due to their lower A V , with fiducial fluxes in the range F 88 fid = 2 − 5 . 2 µ Jy.

claims.hypothesis: Radiation-driven outflows in super-early galaxies like GS-z14-0 eject SN-produced dust to kpc scales, reducing UV attenuation while producing extended FIR continuum emission detectable by ALMA.
claims.experiment: Analytic modeling of dust production, spatial distribution, radiative transfer temperature correction, and rest-frame 88 µm continuum flux as a function of dust extent r_d and dust-to-stellar mass ratio ξ_d, compared against the sensitivity of ALMA DDT 2023.A.00037.S.
claims.result: For GS-z14-0, the fiducial model (ξ_d = 1/529) matching A_V = 0.31 predicts r_d = 1.4 kpc, T_d = 72 K, and F_88^fid = 14.9 µJy (with F_88^max = 40.1 µJy for log ξ_d = -1.6), compared to the ALMA 3σ sensitivity of 18 µJy/beam and resolution of ~0.42"-0.45". Without outflows (r_d = r_e), F_88 is suppressed to 5.3 µJy.
claims.finding: Forthcoming ALMA observations of GS-z14-0 will come very close to constraining the fiducial outflow-based AFM prediction and can clearly discriminate between extended outflow-driven dust and compact/dust-poor scenarios.

evidence.quote: Once applied to the most distant galaxy known, GS-z14-0 at z = 14 . 32, the fiducial model ( ξ d = 1 / 529) predicts F 88 fid = 14 . 9 µ Jy, and a dust extent r d = 1 . 4 kpc.

The results presented below explore both (and additional) possibilities showing that ALMA observations can clearly discriminate between these two alternative scenarios by detecting the FIR dust emission.
Forthcoming ALMA observations, with an expected 3 σ sensitivity of 18 µ Jy, should come very close to constraining the fiducial predictions of the outflow-based attenuation-free model.

claims.hypothesis: If early dust in z > 10 galaxies consists predominantly of large (~0.5 µm) silicate grains from SN ejecta rather than standard MW-like dust, its FIR detectability and spatial extent will be reduced.
claims.experiment: Re-computing the dust temperature and 88 µm flux for GS-z14-0 using optical properties of a log-normal grain size distribution centered at 0.5 µm from Ysard et al. (2019) (κ_UV^large = 5085 cm^2 g^-1, κ_88^large = 15 cm^2 g^-1).
claims.result: Dust temperatures are colder (75 - 85 K at r_e) and the fiducial 88 µm flux for GS-z14-0 drops to F_88^fid = 9.5 µJy at smaller radii.
claims.finding: Large SN dust grains make the galaxy optically thin at more compact radii and yield lower 88 µm fluxes, making ALMA detection more challenging.

evidence.quote: The temperature follows the same trend as in the standard case, but it is significantly colder, reaching at r e values in the range 75 − 85 K. As a result, for any given ξ d , the flux is smaller, e.g. F 88 fid = 9 . 5 µ Jy, and shifted to smaller radii compared to the standard case.

claims.hypothesis: Other spectroscopically confirmed z > 10 galaxies are also candidates for ALMA 88 µm dust continuum detection under the AFM.
claims.experiment: Applying the AFM FIR emission model to GS-z14-1, UNCOVER-z12, GS-z11-0, and GHZ2 using their JWST-measured properties.
claims.result: Predicted fiducial 88 µm fluxes are 2.0 µJy (GS-z14-1), 4.4 µJy (UNCOVER-z12), 5.2 µJy (GS-z11-0), and 3.4 µJy (GHZ2, or 11.2 µJy if A_V = 0.2).
claims.finding: Other known super-early galaxies are significantly fainter at 88 µm due to lower SFRs and attenuations, leaving GS-z14-0 as the most promising target.

evidence.quote: From the Table, we see that the expected fiducial fluxes range from 2 µ Jy for the faintest galaxy (GS-z14-1) to 14.9 µ Jy for the brightest (and most distant) one, GSz14-0; the latter therefore remains the most promising target to constrain the dust content of the very early galaxies.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Compact dust distribution without outflow ejection (r_d = r_e), which either requires an extremely low dust-to-stellar mass ratio (ξ_d = 6.6 x 10^-5) or results in an optically thick regime with suppressed flux (F_88 = 5.3 µJy) and excessive A_V

evidence.quote: Without the outflow hypothesis, to make the galaxy optically thin one should assume an extremely low dust content, corresponding to ξ d = 6 . 6 × 10 − 5 .
The other, more compact solution for the same F 88 , i.e. log( r d /r e ) ≃ 0 . 4, should be discarded because the galaxy would have an A V much larger than observed.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Large silicate grains (~0.5 µm) formed in SN ejecta producing a gray extinction curve

evidence.quote: In addition to dust ejection or destruction by shocks, we need to consider a third possibility, i.e., that early dust is constituted by large, 0 . 1 − 1 µ m size grains.

limitations_admitted.value: The simple analytical model neglects dust self-heating by re-processed thermal photons, dust scattering, and full grain size distributions, which require dedicated numerical radiative transfer simulations.

evidence.quote: For example, the present study does not account for selfheating of the dust by re-processed thermal photons, dust scattering and grain size distribution. The impact of these effects on the results presented here can only be ascertained via dedicated numerical radiative transfer simulations.

referee_caveats_inferred: If the dust is extended to r_d ~ 1.4 kpc (~0.7 arcsec at z=14.32) while the ALMA beam is ~0.42-0.45 arcsec, the emission will be spatially resolved over multiple beams, reducing the peak surface brightness (uJy/beam) relative to the integrated flux F_88 and making a 3-sigma detection harder than a point-source comparison to 18 uJy/beam implies.

There is a minor inconsistency in the stated spatial resolution of DDT 2023.A.00037.S between the Figure 1 caption (0.418") and Section 3 text (0.451"), and in r_d for the fiducial model between Section 2.2 (1.4 kpc) and Section 3 (1.3 kpc).
